en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Gateways to Immeasurable Emanations, Spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Multi-storied Hall of the Great Forest Monastery in Vaiśālī.
In the lecture hall,
he was together with a great assembly of forty thousand bhikṣus.
At that time, the World-Honored One desired to relinquish his life-force.
"In three months' time, I shall enter parinirvāṇa.
He then addressed the Elder Mahāmaudgalyāyana:
"Go and proclaim throughout the trichiliocosm."
The śrāvaka bhikṣus, those on the path of the pratyekabuddhas,
and all the bodhisattvas all came together at the multi-storied lecture hall of the Mahāvana Vihāra.
Maudgalyāyana, having received these instructions, went to the summit of Mount Sumeru.
Entering the *samādhi* of sovereign will (*vaśitā*),
he proclaimed with a great voice throughout the trichiliocosm so that there was none who did not hear and know it.
The Elder Śāriputra then had this thought:

I shall now likewise enter the *yathākāma-vidhi-samādhi* (the concentration of acting according to one's will) and universally exhort all the bhikṣus residing within Jambudvīpa to assemble at the multi-storied lecture hall of the Mahāvana Vihāra.
Having formed this thought, he immediately entered a samādhi according to its form,
universally inviting all bhikṣus who reside in Jambudvīpa to assemble.
At that time, in the multi-storied lecture hall of the Mahāvana Vihāra,
there was an assembly of three million bhikṣus.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One addressed the bodhisattva Akṣayamati and the youth Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
The Bodhisattva Free from Evil Destinies, the Bodhisattva Free from the Darkness of Sorrow,
the Bodhisattva Free from the Obscurations, the Bodhisattva Quieting All Realms,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and the Bodhisattva Fragrant Elephant.
"O Bodhisattva Immeasurable Eloquence and Bodhisattva Maitreya:
you sons of good family, go to the Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions,
and universally inform all the bodhisattvas who are in their last birth before buddhahood."
Bodhisattvas who have attained non-retrogression, those who have attained the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas,
and Bodhisattvas of resolute conviction all gathered at the multi-storied lecture hall of the Great Forest Monastery.
These bodhisattvas then accepted the instruction and acted accordingly.

They went throughout the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and universally announced it to all bodhisattvas who are in their final birth before Buddhahood (*ekajātipratibaddha*),
as well as to those bodhisattvas who have reached the stage of non-retrogression and attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattikadharmakṣānti*).
They all assembled at the multi-storied lecture hall of the Great Forest Monastery (*Mahāvana-vihāra*).
At that time, there were eight billion times one hundred thousand bodhisattvas in their final birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*) in the multi-storied lecture hall of the Great Forest Monastery.
One hundred and ten million attained non-retrogression;
three billion bodhisattvas attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas;
and six billion bodhisattvas attained liberation through faith.
At that time, these great beings assembled together in the multi-storied lecture hall of the Mahāvana Vihāra.
Then, the Venerable Śāriputra saw the great assembly of bodhisattvas gathering like clouds.
He then thought: "I shall, by relying on the Buddha's majestic spiritual power,
respectfully inquire of the World-Honored One so that all bodhisattvas may be freed from the net of doubt and swiftly achieve profound, unimpeded eloquence."
Upon hearing the Dharma taught by all Buddhas throughout the lands of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
they shall retain it in mind without forgetting,
and swiftly attain the unsurpassed, true, and correct path of supreme perfect enlightenment.
Furthermore, it enables Bodhisattvas to attain four inexhaustible gates of pure dharma.
What are these four?
The first is the purity of sentient beings.
Second is the purity of the Dharma;
third is the purity of eloquence;
fourth is the purity of the adornment of the Buddha-field.
One attains four most excellent and harmonious dharmas.
What are these four?
The first is the harmony and serenity of the body.
Second is harmony and joy in speech;
third is harmony and joy in thought;
fourth is harmony and joy in skillful means.
One shall swiftly accomplish four kinds of subtle and wondrous gateways of retention (*dhāraṇī*). What are these four?
The first is called the retention that gives birth to immeasurable gateways.
The second is the retention of the profound patience regarding the Dharma (*gambhīradharmanidhyānākṣānti*).
The third is the retention of skillfulness regarding the faculties of sentient beings (*sattvendriyakuśala*).
The fourth is the retention of skillfulness regarding the causes and effects of sentient beings (*sattvahetuphalakuśala*).
The Venerable Śāriputra reflected:
"This is the bodhisattva’s ground of immeasurable pure wisdom;
I wish for the Buddha to explain it."
He then asked the World-Honored One about this very matter.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One praised Śāriputra, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Śāriputra!"
It is well that you are able to ask such a question for the sake of all bodhisattvas.
Listen attentively, Śāriputra, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well;
I shall now explain the profound merit of the practices of bodhisattvas, by which they swiftly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment.
If Śāriputra wishes to attain all-knowledge and know all phenomena, he should study this gateway and uphold it;
he should study these dhāraṇī-words, namely:
the wordless, the correct word, and the universal word.
Accomplishing the light of eloquence that accords with the Path;
skillfully discerning and ultimately analyzing;
firm in what is spoken, like the *ilā* and *ilī* [of the earth].
Elāpattra Caṇḍa, you have attained the supreme track;
you are immovable and tranquil,
having abandoned all enemies, and your blazing passions are forever extinguished.
Born with an immaculate and pure intrinsic nature,
he skillfully explains that all states of existence are non-existent and without attachment;
he is well-able to subdue and is radiant and free from defilement.
Skillfully maintaining the fruit, he is greatly courageous;
having attained great renown, he moves amidst the unmoving.
Through right movement, he dwells securely in that which is difficult to shake.
They travel in peace and security without obstruction or attachment, opening all dharma-doors;
they act in accordance with what is appropriate, possessing strength and power;
through diligent and courageous effort, they attain the power of skillful means.
Great light universally illuminates and shines forth, stainless;
the mind’s understanding is equanimous, universally penetrating all without exception, reaching everywhere in all matters.
This sublime upholding is that wherein all Buddhas abide.
Thus, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva practices this upholding,
they do not engage in conceptual discrimination regarding the numbered or the unnumbered, nor do they apprehend anything therein.
Regarding all dharmas of abandonment, he advances in merit,
yet there is nothing he does and nothing he does not do;
he perceives no dharma as having conjunction or separation.
There is arising and ceasing,
yet there is no cognition of past, future, or present;
nor does one know whether dharmas possess power or lack power.
In the practice of mindfulness of the Buddha, one does not dwell on the marks and signs,
nor does one dwell on the lineage, nor on the retinue;
there is neither precept, nor concentration, nor wisdom.
There is neither non-understanding nor liberation through the crossing-over of knowledge and vision;
there is no abiding, no attainment, and no exhaustion of afflictions.
One does not know by means of knowing, nor is there non-knowing.
He does not speak of the Dharma as impure for sentient beings;
because there is no "self" and no "other," there is neither dharma, nor discipline, nor proper conduct.
There is no purity, no mindfulness of body, and no mindfulness of mind.
There is no ultimate nirvana,
nor does one dwell upon the past, the future, or the present.
Neither depending on oneself nor depending on others,
one practices non-appropriation toward all phenomena.
Śāriputra, this is called the mindfulness of the Buddha that accords with the grasping of all dharmas.
It is named the subtle meaning of the gate of the fearless upholding that enters into all dharmas;
it is fully equipped with everything desired.
It is named the samādhi of conformity to the single path.
It is also called the root of all virtues;
it is the lineage and the marks and signs obtained not through others,
but produced from one's own dharma.
It is named "Perfect Awakening that Transcends All Demonic Deeds.
Śāriputra, this is the Bodhisattva’s dhāraṇī of giving birth to immeasurable gateways.
Whoever hears this dhāraṇī—
They all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Why is this? Because by upholding this, they will ultimately perfect all the merits of all Buddhas.
He is able to discern all the spheres of conduct of all sentient beings;
because he has attained non-attainment,
he is named "The Sustainer Who Produces Immeasurable Gateways."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"The Dharma is empty and free from doubt; To practice the Way, one must not be heedless.
The nature of phenomena is without forgetfulness or conceptualization; This is the practice through which one attains endurance."
As this sutra has been taught, those who uphold it will never exhaust it;
from this, wondrous wisdom arises, and they swiftly accomplish the unsurpassed path.
If one attains this upholding, the bodhisattva shall have no fear.
The Buddhas of the ten directions preach the Dharma;
Just as it is preached, they hear it all and are able to receive and uphold it all.
With the fullness of both meaning and phrasing, they give rise daily to immeasurable light; Thus does the wisdom that gives birth [to the Dharma] abide.
Even unto the unsurpassed Dharma, all the subtle gateways of dhāraṇī arise from this verse;
one should skillfully protect this sutra,
even if all people were to contemplate it with difficult questions for an entire kalpa.
They are able to resolve all doubts; their wisdom is inexhaustible as they sit near the Unsurpassed Way.
They are true sons of the Dharma King, close and intimate with those who uphold the Dharma, for they constantly keep this sutra in mind.
Respected by all sentient beings, protected by the Buddhas of the ten directions,
and with a reputation that pervades the ten directions— by upholding this sutra,
one shall be able to see eight billion Buddhas at the moment of death.
All shall extend a helping hand to those who uphold this sutra;
even if one has committed various unwholesome deeds over billions of kalpas,
they can be eliminated in a single month by receiving and reciting this sutra.
The merit produced by a Bodhisattva accumulated over billions of eons—
by reciting and upholding this sutra for a single month, one’s power of mindfulness and power of diligence shall equal that,
and one will attain the supreme and wondrous samādhi.
All [realizations] appear before them; they swiftly attain supreme perfect enlightenment.
Among all classes of sentient beings in the three realms, none can act as a Māra to cause interruption for those who practice this sutra.
From him who speaks with truth, from him who possesses the ultimate Dharma,
from him I attained the realization of the Way and reached all-knowledge;
because I formerly heard and upheld this, Dīpaṃkara granted me the prophecy.
All Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, can immediately manifest themselves;
those who wish to hear what the Buddhas of the ten directions have taught will be able to understand it all.
One should single-mindedly practice this dhāraṇī, and all shall swiftly attain accomplishment.
Adorning the Buddha-lands, purifying the assembly,
and perfecting the marks and characteristics as well as the spiritual lineage— all these shall be attained from this sutra;
one should eliminate mental laxity and contemplate with single-minded focus for seven days.
Eight billion buddhas have come together to bestow this sutra:
It is not conceivable by thought, nor is it conceivable through non-thought;
This very thought is itself non-thought, And from this, one swiftly attains accomplishment.
Venerate this scripture; do not harbor doubts regarding the Path.
Just as one should not doubt that the great ocean lacks jewels, so too, for the sake of bringing peace to all devas and humans, no aspiration shall be difficult to fulfill.
This is for the sake of generating the bodhicitta; one should simply practice with correct intention.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva accomplishes four dharmas.
One will swiftly attain this dhāraṇī.
What are the four? They are:
weariness with and detachment from sensual desires.
Without giving rise to thoughts of haste,
they bestow all that exists upon all sentient beings;
day and night they seek the Dharma with a mind free from weariness or indolence.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Those who are weary of and detached from sensual desires, Yet still create manifold evils through negligence— the conditions for the realm of Māra and the hells—
Such evils cause one to fall into the evil paths."
One does not give rise to envy toward others; one does not act for the sake of fame.
One regards sentient beings with compassion and love.
Even when noble, dignified, or handsome beings provoke resentment and strife, all such things have greed as their root.
Therefore, one should abandon craving; by abandoning craving, one achieves the sublime restraint.
Constantly delighting in the Dharma day and night, those who investigate with discernment, who seek the path, and who strive with single-minded diligence, shall swiftly achieve the sublime restraint.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
there are four other dharmas by which a bodhisattva accomplishes and swiftly attains this dhāraṇī.
What are the four?
Dwelling in seclusion with a tranquil mind,
and attaining profound *dharmakṣānti*.
He does not seek gain or offerings;
he gives away all things, both internal and external, without exception.
These are the four.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:

"Dwelling in seclusion with tranquil resolve is praised by the Buddha; Guarding oneself in empty stillness, one does not disparage others, But constantly delights in cultivating the profound patience of the Dharma (dharmanidhyānakṣānti).
Like one whose head is on fire, one must never be heedless."
Seeking neither fame nor gain, he thus practices all manner of guileless conduct;
Content everywhere like a flying bird, he disciplines his body and diminishes himself to cultivate virtuous deeds.
How joyful it is to have attained the Buddha’s teaching— To leave the household life and receive the full precepts!
Having left home and departed from all suffering, one follows and practices the Buddha’s teaching.
If one does not obtain the Buddha’s teaching, then the benefits of the precepts for those who have gone forth—
faith, morality, generosity, learning, and wisdom— will all fail to be accomplished.
This fault keeps one far removed from the Buddha; therefore, one should abandon greed for profit.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are four other dharmas of a bodhisattva.
One will achieve and swiftly attain this dhāraṇī.
What are the four?
First, these eight syllables encompass all meanings according to their significance; they enter into them all.
The eight characters are *paropagaṭaśakṣa*.
*Pa* signifies the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*);
all phenomena (*dharmas*), being without self (*anātman*), enter through this gateway.
*La* refers to the marks and signs being signless,
just as the body of the Tathāgata enters into the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).
*Ba* refers to the dharmas of ignorance and the dharmas of wisdom.
It is the meaning of entering in accordance with reality.
"Ka" refers to the ultimate meaning of entering in accordance with the results of karmic actions, as well as those that are not the results of karmic actions.
All such matters are fully and completely encompassed within this meaning of entering in accordance with reality.
*Ja* signifies that birth, the conditions for aging and death, and all things whatsoever enter into neither arising nor ceasing.
*Dha* signifies that all dhāraṇīs enter into emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
*Sā* means that all dhāraṇīs follow and enter [this].
*Kṣa* means that all phenomena are entirely included within suchness (*tathatā*).
These eight syllables encompass the full meaning within them.
Second, to skillfully transcribe this sutra and uphold it without abandoning it;
third, to recite and study this sutra every half-month;
fourth, to provide offerings and support to those who uphold this sutra.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"One should contemplate the meaning of these eight words;
skillfully copy and uphold this sutra, and recite it once every half-month, exhorting those who practice and uphold it to proceed."

In all the lands throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, immeasurable Buddhas sit before them at the site of enlightenment, their wondrous marks perfected; one should diligently practice this dhāraṇī-conduct.
Furthermore, Śāriputra:
A bodhisattva who studies and maintains this obtains four kinds of meritorious benefits. What are the four?
First, they are kept in mind by all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Second, they will be free from all demonic activities.
Third, their obstructive karmic hindrances of evil and transgression will swiftly become purified.
Fourth, they will fully accomplish unimpeded eloquence and analytical discernment.
These are the four.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"The Buddhas always protect and keep them in mind; the various Māras find no opportunity."
All karmic obstacles of sin are completely eliminated, and one attains the wondrous and immeasurable dhāraṇī.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"In the past, incalculable kalpas ago..."

There was a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Ratnaśikhin-jvālā-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Leader, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
Śāriputra, when that Tathāgata Ratnaśikhin was approaching his parinirvāṇa,
there was a wheel-turning king named Dharaniprabha who ruled over the four continents with complete sovereignty.
The king had a crown prince named Wunian Dedao (Anutpādaguṇamārga).
At the time of his birth, his form was like that of a sixteen-year-old youth.
From that World-Honored One, he heard this dhāraṇī.
Having heard and upheld this, he applied himself with single-minded diligence to its study;
for seven thousand years he was not overcome by sleep,
and during those seven thousand years he never once gave rise to a craving for physical rest.
He never thought of royal affairs.
Furthermore, during those seven thousand years, his body did not lean toward reclining;
he remained seated upright in meditative absorption (*samādhi*). Thereupon, he beheld ninety billion nayutas of Buddhas.
Having heard the Dharma from him, they were all able to receive and uphold it;
they then left the household life to study the Path.
For ninety thousand years, by means of these immeasurable gateways for generating and upholding [the teachings], they extensively expounded them for others.
During the course of a single lifetime, they bring eighty billion nayutas of people to accomplishment,
establishing them in the mind set on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
exhorting, instructing, and transforming them so that they do not regress.
At that time, there was among the assembly a son of a householder named Candradhvaja.
Having heard this upholding [of the Dharma], he followed it with a sincere heart and rejoiced.
By virtue of the causes and conditions of those roots of goodness from his rejoicing, [he attained great merit].
He constantly attained proximity to ninety billion Buddhas;
he obtained the supreme dhāraṇī, the supreme station, and immeasurable eloquence.
Furthermore, for three kalpas, he remained in proximity to all the Buddhas.
At the end of the third eon, Candradhvaja attained Buddhahood under the name Dīpāṅkara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
At that time, the prince named Amoghadarśin was none other than the present Amitāyus Buddha of the western quarter.
Śāriputra, I too, along with the bodhisattvas of this Bhadrakalpa, have heard this dhāraṇī in the past;
having heard it, I rejoiced in it.
By virtue of the causal conditions of these roots of goodness from such rejoicing, [I have attained this].
They eliminate the offenses of birth and death for four hundred thousand kalpas and further attain proximity to ninety billion Buddhas. Therefore,
Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva...
Those who wish to swiftly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* should diligently rejoice in this sublime dhāraṇī.
[By doing so,] they will obtain the merit of such rejoicing.
Even for a Bodhisattva on the stage of non-retrogression, this serves as a great causal condition;
how much more so for those who copy, uphold, receive, recite, and practice according to the teaching.
No people whatsoever are able to conceive of or describe the extent of their merit.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“Those who hear this sutra and rejoice in their hearts, Who copy, uphold, revere, and recite it—
The measure of the karmic reward for such celestial and human beings Cannot be calculated.”
In every birth they constantly see the Buddhas; with faith and inclination, they do not waver.
Having realized the essential points of the profound Dharma, they swiftly awaken to the Unsurpassed Way.
Their samādhis never decline, and they master the gates of the three vidyās and dhāraṇīs.
Wealth and beauty, and the constant vision of Buddhas, up to the unsurpassed path—
recalling past lives, the son of a householder heard and retained [this teaching],
and immediately beheld ninety billion nayutas of Buddhas.
Whatever one seeks shall be fulfilled according to one's wish, and the unsurpassed path will be attained.
If one desires to swiftly achieve Buddhahood, to subdue the hosts of Māras through the power of the Way,
and to perfect the hundred marks of merit, there is no difficulty in practicing this.
Even if one were to fill buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges with jewels and offer them in charity,
it would still not equal the merit of writing out or upholding this sutra.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva practices and maintains this [sutra],...
There are eight great spirits who are deities of the Snowy Mountains;
they together protect and watch over him.
Their names are the Spirit Courageous and Strong and the Spirit of Great Power.
The Lord Maheśvara, the Heroic and Fierce God,
the God who Knows Conduct,
the Invincible God, Kumāra, and the God Subāhu.
These are the eight.
If he wishes to cause the various deities to come,
he should bathe his body and purify his clothing.
Maintaining a correct countenance, he walked with mindful attention and compassionately reflected upon sentient beings;
as he contemplated these essential teachings according to his recollection,
those deities immediately appeared before him.
Furthermore, there are eight bodhisattvas born in the Heaven of Desire-Practice who also constantly protect and mindfully sustain him.
What are these eight?
The Celestial Son Illuminating the Ten Directions, the Celestial Son Who Practices Detachment from Desire,
the Celestial Son Radiance of Wisdom, the Celestial Son Sun-like,
the Celestial Son True Reality, and the Celestial Son Fulfilled Vow.
The Celestial King Star-King knows the Celestial King Practice-Knowing;
these constitute the eight.
These bodhisattvas constantly come to protect and mindfully guard [the practitioner].
Cause them to apply themselves with single-minded diligence so that they may swiftly attain this sublime dhāraṇī.
For those who practice this dhāraṇī, truthfulness is the foundation;
they should always remain respectful and mindful of the kindness [bestowed].
They study the profound *dharmakṣānti* and contemplate the dharmas that are neither arising nor ceasing.
They maintain the precepts with equanimity, protecting both themselves and others.
When this Dharma was being taught, thirty-two *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* numbers of bodhisattvas immediately attained this retention (*dhāraṇī*).
They did not regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Six hundred thousand people attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Thirty-two thousand gods and humans [also attained it].
All of them resolved their minds upon the unsurpassed, perfect, and true path to enlightenment.
At that time, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways,
and the heavens rained down various flowers that covered the entire world.
The heavens sent forth musical instruments that resounded spontaneously without being struck.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, what should this sutra be named?"
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"The essential name of this sutra is 'The Retention that Produces Immeasurable Gateways,' and it is also called 'The Path-Practice of the Stage of One Birth Remaining'."
It is also called "Attaining the Way, Subduing Māra, and Obtaining All-Knowledge.
You should uphold it.
While this Dharma was being spoken, the Venerable Śāriputra—
The bodhisattvas who had gathered from the ten directions,
as well as the entire assembly of devas, humans, gandharvas, asuras, and others,
were all filled with great joy upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken.
The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Gateways to the Birth of the Immeasurable Spoken by the Buddha.
